messages:
Maria: Quick Q — I converted from contractor -> FT on 2024-04-10 and missed the beginning of open enrollment. I need to add my domestic partner to health + dental and opt into voluntary life. County registration for our domestic partnership is queued but not yet processed. Can we add them retroactive to 4/10? Also curious about payroll proration and any required docs.

Zoe (People Ops): Congrats on the role change! 
You have a 30-day special enrollment window from your FT effective date (4/10) to submit elections. If you enroll in that window we can set coverage effective 4/10. We will need proof of partnership — the CA registration is easiest, but we accept alternates temporarily (see below). Voluntary life typically can be added as a QLE; some amounts may require EOI.

Ben (Payroll): If coverage is effective 4/10 and you enroll within 30 days, premiums will be prorated from the effective date. Our payroll runs on the last calendar day of the month; your first deduction will likely show on the 4/30 run. I'll confirm cents/rounding.

Maria: If county processing runs past 30 days, can I provide an in-progress receipt + affidavit so coverage isn't denied?

Zoe (People Ops): We can accept temporary documentation: a dated application/receipt from the county + two corroborating docs (shared lease, joint bank stmt, or utilities) + a signed domestic-partner affidavit. Final registration must be uploaded within 60 days to keep retroactive effective date. If not received within 60 days we may need to reverse coverage. I'll DM you the checklist and the affidavit template. :slightly_smiling_face:

hr-bot: Reminder — special enrollment deadline: 30 days from status change. Upload link: https://benefits.redwood.internal/upload (internal).

James (Legal): Quick note on voluntary life and HSA: voluntary life midyear is allowed with status change but higher coverage could require Evidence of Insurability. For HSA: if your partner has other coverage that is NOT HSA-eligible (eg. non-HDHP), it may affect whether you can contribute. Please confirm partner's current plan type.

Maria: Partner has a small-employer plan that is HSA-eligible. So HSA probably ok? Who coordinates that verification?

Zoe (People Ops): OK — if partner's plan is HSA-eligible that typically doesn't block your HSA. We'll have Benefits Ops validate the partner plan type during enrollment. Please note: if we confirm partner has non-compatible coverage later, we may have to adjust HSA elections retroactively.

Ben (Payroll): Sample proration calc (example):
```
Monthly premium = $200
Days in month = 30
Effective date = 2024-04-10 -> active days = 21
Prorated premium = 200 * 21/30 = $140
```
Actual deduction may vary by a few cents due to rounding and payroll period alignment. I'll post the exact deduction estimate after I run your payroll case.

Maria: Awesome — thanks. Also, does voluntary life for partner require SSN on file? We don't have their SSN scanned yet (they're not local).

Zoe (People Ops): For life insurance we usually need name, DOB, and proof of identity; SSN is preferable but in some cases we can proceed with other ID plus a follow-up SSN upload within 60 days. If EOI is required, the insurer will specify additional docs. I'll flag this to the carrier rep.

Zoe (People Ops): Next steps for you: 1) I will open a benefits case and DM you the provisional enrollment link + affidavit. 2) Upload county receipt + 2 corroborating docs in the 30-day window to get 4/10 effective date. 3) Ben will post proration estimate and confirm payroll timing. 4) Benefits Ops will validate partner plan/HSA interplay and confirm EOI requirements for voluntary life.

Ben (Payroll): I'll have the proration estimate in ~24h and attach a mock payroll screenshot.

Maria: Perfect — really appreciate the help! :heart:
